key_insight: M3-Score evaluates radiology generative models on three separate axes—fidelity, memorization, and coverage—using radiology-specific encoder features instead of one summary score.
clinical_relevance: This could make it easier to compare synthetic radiology images in ways that better reflect clinically meaningful similarity, diversity, and overfitting risk.
method: Uses a frozen radiology-pretrained vision transformer (RadioDINO-s16) as the feature encoder.
Computes fidelity with unbiased multi-bandwidth RBF MMD² at the final encoder block.
Computes memorization with nearest-neighbor distance at 75% depth and coverage with k-NN radius coverage at 33% depth.
evidence_signal: On BraTS brain MRI, the fidelity axis ranked five comparison sets perfectly (Spearman ρ=1.00), a diffusion model covered only 38% of the real distribution, and RadioDINO features separated real vs generated samples better than InceptionV3 or CLIP (ROC-AUC 0.819 vs 0.555 and 0.582).
watch_item: Results are based on a specific radiology encoder and one dataset, so generalization to other modalities, scanners, and clinical tasks still needs validation.
paper_title: M3-Score: Fidelity, Memorization and Coverage as Separate Axes for Evaluating Generative Radiology Image Models
